claims.text: The investigated alloy is an as-cast equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy.
The equimolar refractory-element mixture produces severe lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr locally reduces the Peierls barrier.
The reduced Peierls barrier enhances dislocation mobility at high temperature.
Greater dislocation mobility produces a more homogeneous distribution of dislocations.
More homogeneous dislocation-mediated deformation promotes homogeneous plastic flow.
Reduced strain localization delays crack initiation.
At about 1200°C, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than commercially used pure tungsten under identical loading.
At about 1200°C, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater toughness than commercially used pure tungsten under identical loading.
The WTaTiVZr alloy will have a lower critical resolved shear stress than pure tungsten at about 1200°C.
The WTaTiVZr alloy will develop a more uniform dislocation network than pure tungsten during high-temperature deformation.
Increasing temperature and reducing strain rate can improve deformation performance in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed mechanism may not dominate at lower temperatures or under qualitatively different loading conditions.
Dynamic recovery or recrystallization could contribute to high-temperature deformation and confound attribution to lattice distortion.
Testing WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten at identical temperature and loading conditions provides the proposed controlled comparison.
Failure to observe the specified shear-stress reduction, dislocation homogeneity, or correlation between mobility and lattice distortion would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says either absence of reduced shear resistance or absence of a more homogeneous network is sufficient for falsification, whereas the formal rule generally joins those failures with 'and' and separately adds lack of correlation. The logical criteria for falsification are therefore inconsistent.
